messages.subject: Prediction map on occurrence
parts:
Dear all, 

I am analyzing a count data with lots of zero, so I developed a zero-inflated method. 

A part of code as following:

z <- yp$count>0 +0
y <- ifelse(yp$count>0,yp$count,NA)

# INLA formula 
form <-  y ~ 0 + z.b0 + depth.z + secchi.z + geartemp.z + do_gear.z + geardepth.z + f(sz, model=spde, replicate=sz.repl) + y.b0 + depth.y + secchi.y + geartemp.y + do_gear.y + geardepth.y + f(sy, copy='sz', replicate=sy.repl,fixed=FALSE)

result.zinb <- inla(form,family=c("binomial","zeroinflatednbinomial2"),
                    data=inla.stack.data(stk.zy),
                    control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(stk.zy),compute=TRUE,link=inla.stack.data(stk.zy)$link),
                    control.inla=list(strategy='gaussian'),
                    control.fixed = list(prec.intercept=1))

The "binomial" part allowed me to analyze the probability of occurrence. However, I got a prediction map on z as attached, with predicted values ranges from -8 to 6. I think the predicted values should locate in [0, 1]. Is there any comments on my results?

Thank you,
Ruby

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Prediction map on occurrence
parts:
Precisely which part of the output did you use for plotting?
If you've specified the "link" information correctly (your are supplying something, but didn't show your stack setup) then fitted.values will have the link function applied. linear.predictor never does. So you should be plotting fitted.values.

Finn
